title: Vegetarian Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: Lentil and root vegetable filling under a golden mash crust
excerpt: Vegetarian shepherd's pie replaces lamb mince with green or brown lentils and diced root vegetables in a rich, well-seasoned gravy under mash. The lentils give the filling the dense texture and body that makes the dish satisfying as a main course. This is not a pallid substitute; it stands on its own.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze assembled and unbaked. Defrost overnight, then bake at 180°C fan for 35 minutes from cold.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze one. It reheats well and the flavour improves the next day.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead. Top, cover, and refrigerate. Bake from the fridge with 10 extra minutes.

content.text: Vegetarian shepherd's pie works because green lentils hold their texture in a braise the way mince does, and absorb the stock and Worcestershire sauce without turning to mush. The secret is to use a generous amount of tomato puree and umami seasoning to build depth in the gravy, and to cook the vegetables until they are soft but still distinct. The mash on top behaves exactly as it does on a meat pie.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook {{onion}} chopped onion, {{carrot}} diced carrots, and {{celery}} diced celery for 10 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, the rosemary, and the thyme. Cook for 1 minute.

Add {{chestnut-mushrooms}} of mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes until their liquid has evaporated. Stir in {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add {{green-lentils}} of rinsed lentils, {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce, and {{stock-vegetable}} of stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes until the lentils are tender and the gravy has thickened. Season well.
Boil {{potato}} of potato chunks in salted water until tender, about 18 minutes. Drain, steam dry, and mash with {{unsalted-butter}} of butter and {{whole-milk}} of warm milk. Season.

Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Spoon the lentil filling into a baking dish. Spread the mash on top and rough it up with a fork. Scatter over the grated cheddar if using. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden.

items.cause: Lentils on their own are bland. Without confident seasoning and umami ingredients, the filling lacks depth.
items.fix: Add more tomato puree (it carries umami), check the stock is well-seasoned, and increase the Worcestershire sauce. Taste at the end and adjust.

items.symptom: The lentils are still firm after 30 minutes
items.cause: Old dried lentils take longer to cook; salted water slows cooking too.
items.fix: Do not add salt to the filling until the lentils are tender. Old lentils can take 45 minutes. Check your packet date.

items.symptom: The filling is watery under the mash
items.cause: The stock did not reduce enough before baking.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered until the filling holds together on a spoon with little free liquid. It will loosen slightly in the oven.

items.symptom: The mash sinks into the lentils during baking
items.cause: The filling was too loose or too warm when the mash went on.
items.fix: The filling should be thick and cooled to room temperature before the mash is spread on top.

content.text: The vegetarian shepherd's pie became a staple of British home cooking as lentils moved from wholefood shops into mainstream kitchens in the 1980s and 1990s. Unlike many early vegetarian adaptations of classic dishes, this one has genuine staying power because lentils respond to long cooking in much the same way as meat. It is one of the most made weeknight dishes in British vegetarian households.
